findings.title: cancelOrder calls dynamodb:DeleteItem on orders, but aws_iam_role.api_role doesn't allow it
findings.detail: src/api/app.js:23 calls dynamodb:DeleteItem on aws_dynamodb_table.orders. The Lambda aws_lambda_function.api runs as aws_iam_role.api_role, whose policies don't grant that action on this resource, so the call fails with AccessDenied at runtime.

findings.title: aws_iam_role.api_role allows s3:* on everything, but the code uses only s3:PutObject on aws_s3_bucket.uploads, legacy-reports
findings.detail: aws_iam_role_policy.api_access (statement 2) grants s3:* on all resources (*). The code that runs as this role uses s3:PutObject on aws_s3_bucket.uploads, legacy-reports. Narrowing the policy to what is used limits the damage if the function is compromised.

findings.title: "legacy-reports" (s3) is hardcoded in code but not defined in your infrastructure code
findings.detail: src/api/app.js:28 (s3:PutObject). No resource of this type in the analyzed infrastructure code has that name, so changes to it can't be reviewed or reproduced and it may have drifted.

sourceFiles.src/worker/main.py:
import json
import os

import boto3

dynamodb = boto3.resource("dynamodb")
sqs = boto3.client("sqs")
table = dynamodb.Table(os.environ["TABLE_NAME"])


def process(record):
    order = json.loads(record["body"])
    table.put_item(Item=order)


def handler(event, context):
    for record in event["Records"]:
        process(record)
    sqs.receive_message(QueueUrl=os.environ["QUEUE_URL"], MaxNumberOfMessages=1)
